description.narrative: Ambassaden mottog ett projektförslag från IGAD:s jämställdhetssavdelning i oktober 2022. Det föreslagna programmet syftar till att förbättra IGAD:s institutionella kapacitet för jämställdhetsintegrering. Projektet kommer att använda digitala och andra verktyg för att öka medvetenheten och mätbarheten kring jämställdhetsintegrering inom IGAD:S olika typer av interventioner. Lärdomarna från projektet förväntas sedan kunna användas i sambarbetet andra REC:s som Sverige ger stöd till. Projektet planeras att pågå i tre år, från juli 2023 till juni 2026, med en total budget om 21 MSEK. Projektets övergripande mål är att skapa institutionella metoder som är fira från diskriminerande fördomar och stereotyper och som kan användas inom IGAD och dess olika programverksamheter. Målet är vidare att öka IGAD:s institutionella kapacitet när det gäller systemuppbyggnad, att bidra till den interna förståelsen av jämställdhetsfrågor, och att förbättra jämställdhetsintegreringen inom IGAD:s egna program.

The Embassy received a request for support from IGAD’s gender affairs department in October 2022. The proposed program aims to enhance IGAD Institutional capacity of gender mainstreaming and attaining gender equality. The project will use key digital elements, awareness raising mechanisms and tools that increase accountability of all IGAD divisions to enable attaining better gender related results of other interventions of IGAD. The learning from this intervention is expected to be mainstreamed to other RECs that are supported by Sweden. The total budget of the project is 21 MSEK for the period of three years, from July 2023 to June 2026. The goal of the program is to create gender equitable institutional practices that are free from gender related biases and stereotyping in IGAD and IGAD program interventions as an organization and at member States level to effectively address gender inequality. The overall objective of this intervention is to enhance institutional capacity of IGAD in terms of system building and staff awareness raising and improving gender mainstreaming across IGAD programs.

Objective of the intervention
The IGAD project on Institutional Capacity Strengthening of IGAD on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment (GEWE) is designed with a premise that institutional capacity building will lead to organizational transformation and gender responsiveness.
The project has the following two overarching and interrelated outcomes:
1. System, clear approach, and strategy in place in IGAD Secretariat and specialized offices for result and evidence-based gender equality and women empowerment interventions.
2. Systematic coordination and gender equitable organizational culture among IGAD divisions in place for promoting the IGAD Gender Equality agenda in an effective and sustainable manner.
The two outcomes were intended to be achieved through four key outputs which were:
1.1. Increased capacity of IGAD to implement the Regional Gender Strategy:
1.2.: Increased capacity of IGAD Secretariat and specialized office sub offices to promote Gender equality institutionally and in programme intervention
1.3: Regional gender transformative Leadership Academy and Gender Knowledge hub established.
2.1: Increased capacity of IGAD on coordination, gender equitable organizational culture and gender management systems

The main results of the IGAD Institutional Capacity Strengthening on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment (GEWE) project during the first half of the second year of the project (from July to December 2024) which are reflected on the semiannual report include.
- The launch of the Gender Management Systems (GMS) Handbook and the development of a customized Gender Mainstreaming Toolkit, which have enhanced staff understanding and operationalization of gender equality strategies within IGAD
-Engagement of a consultant to conduct a comprehensive capacity needs assessment involving over 50 staff members across IGAD divisions, providing critical insights to inform further institutional reforms.
- Completion of a gender-responsive leadership curriculum for the IGAD Leadership Academy (ILA), aimed at building leadership capacity on gender issues. The ILA is implementing a comprehensive and inclusive curriculum designed with input from local and international experts.
- Conducted a training on Gender-Responsive Human Resources Management, Staff Appraisal Mechanisms, and Procurement, improving staff skills to embed gender considerations into recruitment, procurement, and workplace policies.
- Unexpected result achieved during the reporting period was the Revitalization of the IGAD Women, Peace, and Security Forum (IWPSF), which has led to better coordination, including establishing a regional reporting mechanism, adopting standardized reporting templates aligned with continental frameworks and electing new leadership to advance gender-sensitive peace processes.
These accomplishments collectively contribute to strengthening IGADs institutional capacity to promote gender equality and womens empowerment across its programs and member states.
